shortAnswer: You usually do not need to give up cola completely. A manufacturer example lists 34 mg of caffeine in a 330 ml Coca-Cola; count the exact drink toward the usual pregnancy limit of less than 200 mg a day.
why: Caffeine from cola, coffee, tea, chocolate and medicines adds together. Brand, recipe and serving size can change the amount, so the package in your hand matters more than a remembered number.

alternatives.label: Closest taste
alternatives.title: Caffeine-free cola
alternatives.note: Keeps the familiar cola taste without using part of the daily caffeine allowance.

alternatives.label: Keep the original
alternatives.title: A smaller serving
alternatives.note: Choose a size you can count easily and include it with every other caffeine source that day.

alternatives.label: Fresh option
alternatives.title: Sparkling water with citrus
alternatives.note: Cold, fizzy and easy to vary with lemon, lime, orange or mint.

labelCheck: “Zero sugar” does not mean caffeine-free. Look specifically for “caffeine-free” and check the serving size.

shortAnswer: Coffee can stay if all caffeine for the day remains below 200 mg. Café size, bean, brew method and extra espresso shots can make two similar-looking drinks very different.
why: The limit applies to the whole day, not to coffee alone. Tea, cola, chocolate, energy drinks and some medicines can also contribute.

alternatives.label: Closest ritual
alternatives.title: Decaf coffee
alternatives.note: Keeps the cup, aroma and café routine with much less caffeine, though decaf is not always completely caffeine-free.

alternatives.label: Gentle step down
alternatives.title: Half-caf
alternatives.note: Mix regular and decaf or ask the café for one regular shot and one decaf shot.

alternatives.label: Keep the original
alternatives.title: A smaller, single-shot drink
alternatives.note: Ask how many shots it contains and leave room in the daily total for tea, cola or chocolate.

labelCheck: Do not estimate from cup colour or drink name. Check the volume and number of espresso shots; bottled coffee should list caffeine on its label when available.

shortAnswer: Choose a different drink during pregnancy unless your doctor has reviewed the exact product. Energy drinks can make caffeine easy to underestimate and may add other stimulant ingredients.
why: A generic caffeine total cannot assess every stimulant blend, herbal extract or concentrated ingredient. “Natural energy” is not a pregnancy-safety statement.

alternatives.label: Cold and fizzy
alternatives.title: Caffeine-free sparkling drink
alternatives.note: Choose one without an energy, stimulant or herbal blend and check the full ingredient list.

alternatives.label: With food
alternatives.title: Water plus a regular snack
alternatives.note: A drink and a snack containing carbohydrate and protein may help when the real need is hydration or food.

alternatives.label: When exhaustion persists
alternatives.title: Ask about the fatigue
alternatives.note: Severe or ongoing tiredness deserves care rather than repeatedly masking it with stimulants.

labelCheck: Check caffeine per container, not only per serving, and look for guarana, stimulant blends, concentrated extracts and pre-workout wording.

shortAnswer: Choose an alcohol-free drink during pregnancy. There is no known safe amount, safe time or safe type of alcohol in pregnancy.
why: Changing the type of alcohol does not remove the pregnancy risk. The useful swap is the same occasion and flavour style without alcohol.

alternatives.label: Closest occasion
alternatives.title: A clearly labelled 0.0% drink
alternatives.note: Use the label rather than the front-of-pack style; “low alcohol” and “alcohol-free” definitions can differ.

alternatives.label: Restaurant order
alternatives.title: A made-to-order no-alcohol mocktail
alternatives.note: Ask for no bitters or alcoholic flavourings and choose pasteurized juices.

alternatives.label: Simple at home
alternatives.title: Sparkling water and pasteurized juice
alternatives.note: Serve cold in the same glass with citrus or herbs for the ritual without alcohol.

labelCheck: Look for 0.0% when you want the clearest substitute. Check kombucha and fermented drinks too; the name alone does not tell you the alcohol content.

shortAnswer: Keep the meal, change the filling: choose cooked seafood, cooked protein or vegetarian sushi instead of raw fish or raw shellfish.
why: The practical pregnancy issue is the raw ingredient and food handling, not the rice, seaweed or shape of the dish.

alternatives.label: Closest order
alternatives.title: Cooked salmon, shrimp or crab-style roll
alternatives.note: Confirm the seafood is fully cooked and the roll is made with clean utensils.

alternatives.label: No seafood
alternatives.title: Avocado, cucumber or cooked-vegetable roll
alternatives.note: Ask for fresh preparation and clean separation from raw fish if cross-contact worries you.

alternatives.label: Same bowl format
alternatives.title: Poke bowl with fully cooked protein
alternatives.note: Use fresh washed vegetables and a cooked topping rather than raw fish or raw egg.

labelCheck: “Smoked,” “seared” and “marinated” do not always mean cooked through. Ask how the filling was prepared.

item: Deli meat, cured meat and hot dogs
shortAnswer: The easy general swap is heat: have deli meat or a hot dog steaming hot instead of cold from the refrigerator.
why: Heating changes a cold ready-to-eat product into a lower-risk option while keeping the sandwich, pizza or hot-dog meal familiar.

alternatives.label: Keep the filling
alternatives.title: A hot toasted sandwich
alternatives.note: Heat the meat until steaming throughout, then assemble and eat promptly.

alternatives.label: Freshly cooked
alternatives.title: Chicken, turkey, beef or pork
alternatives.note: Use meat cooked through and served hot rather than chilled pre-sliced meat.

alternatives.label: Meat-free
alternatives.title: A hot bean or cooked-vegetable filling
alternatives.note: Choose a freshly prepared filling and keep cold ingredients properly chilled.

labelCheck: Microwaving briefly is not enough if the centre stays cool. The practical check is steaming hot throughout.

shortAnswer: For the simplest general choice, use pasteurized hard or semi-hard cheese. If choosing a soft or mould-ripened cheese, check the exact product and use pregnancy guidance from your care team; cooking until steaming hot can make some dishes a better option.
why: Cheese advice depends on milk treatment, moisture, rind, storage and whether the food is thoroughly cooked. “Soft” alone is not a complete safety label.

alternatives.label: Simplest cold swap
alternatives.title: Pasteurized cheddar, gouda or another firm cheese
alternatives.note: Check that it is pasteurized and keep it refrigerated within its use-by date.

alternatives.label: For a hot dish
alternatives.title: Cheese cooked until steaming
alternatives.note: Use it in a dish that becomes steaming hot throughout, not only warmed at the edges.

alternatives.label: For creamy texture
alternatives.title: Pasteurized cream cheese or cottage cheese
alternatives.note: Check the label, refrigeration and use-by date before eating it cold.

labelCheck: Check “pasteurized,” the cheese type, storage instructions and use-by date. Pasteurization does not replace safe refrigeration and handling.

shortAnswer: The universal cautious swap is a fully cooked egg or a product made with pasteurized egg instead of a runny or raw egg.
why: Cooking the white and yolk through, or using pasteurized egg, lowers foodborne-infection risk without removing eggs from the menu.

alternatives.label: Same breakfast
alternatives.title: Egg cooked until white and yolk are firm
alternatives.note: Fry, boil, poach or scramble it until no raw or runny part remains.

alternatives.label: For sauces
alternatives.title: Commercial pasteurized-egg mayonnaise
alternatives.note: Check the ingredients and refrigeration instructions; do not assume a homemade sauce uses pasteurized egg.

alternatives.label: For baking
alternatives.title: A fully baked version
alternatives.note: Do not taste raw batter; bake until the centre is properly cooked.

labelCheck: Country-specific egg schemes can differ. If the package does not clearly support a local exception, use the fully cooked or pasteurized option.

shortAnswer: Choose a version made without alcohol and with pasteurized egg—or a dessert that is fully baked instead.
why: Two separate details can matter in the same dessert: raw egg and alcohol. Removing only one does not answer the other.

alternatives.label: Closest version
alternatives.title: Pasteurized-egg, alcohol-free tiramisu or mousse
alternatives.note: Ask about both ingredients; “homemade” does not reveal whether the egg is pasteurized.

alternatives.label: Easy restaurant order
alternatives.title: A fully baked cake or pudding
alternatives.note: Check that it has no alcoholic soak, sauce or uncooked egg topping.

alternatives.label: Cold option
alternatives.title: Pasteurized yogurt with fruit
alternatives.note: Keeps a creamy, chilled dessert format with an ingredient list that is easier to verify.

labelCheck: Ask separately: “Does it contain alcohol?” and “Are the eggs pasteurized or fully cooked?” Coffee-flavoured desserts may also add caffeine.

shortAnswer: Choose cooked lower-mercury fish instead of large predatory fish. Exact species names and local contamination advisories vary, so check local guidance for the fish you buy or catch.
why: The goal is not to avoid all fish. It is to keep the nutritional benefits while reducing mercury exposure and foodborne-infection risk.

alternatives.label: Oily-fish option
alternatives.title: Cooked salmon or sardines
alternatives.note: Choose a lower-mercury variety, cook thoroughly and vary the fish you eat.

alternatives.label: Mild option
alternatives.title: Cooked shrimp or a lower-mercury white fish
alternatives.note: Confirm the species when possible and cook until fully done.

alternatives.label: Caught locally
alternatives.title: Check the water-specific advisory
alternatives.note: A local warning can override a general list because contamination differs by waterway.

labelCheck: Fish names can vary by market. Check the exact species, serving advice and any local catch warning—not only “tuna” or “white fish.”

shortAnswer: Check the exact ingredient list before making an herbal or wellness blend a daily pregnancy drink. “Herbal,” “detox” and “natural” do not establish pregnancy safety.
why: Blends may combine several herbs, concentrated extracts or supplement-like doses. A familiar food ingredient is different from a medicinal-dose product.

alternatives.label: Warm and simple
alternatives.title: Hot water with lemon
alternatives.note: Uses a familiar food ingredient without a multi-herb or concentrated wellness blend.

alternatives.label: Tea ritual
alternatives.title: Decaf black tea
alternatives.note: It usually contains much less caffeine than regular tea, but still count any caffeine shown on the pack.

alternatives.label: Keep the blend
alternatives.title: Photograph the label for review
alternatives.note: Ask a doctor or pharmacist about the exact ingredients, dose and how often you drink it.

labelCheck: Read every ingredient and the serving directions. Avoid treating a tea as harmless because it is caffeine-free or sold as food.

shortAnswer: Choose sprouts cooked thoroughly rather than raw. Washing alone may not remove bacteria growing inside the sprout.
why: This is one of the cases where rinsing is not the full fix. Heat is the useful change.

alternatives.label: Keep the ingredient
alternatives.title: Sprouts cooked until steaming
alternatives.note: Add them early enough in a stir-fry, soup or noodle dish to cook thoroughly.

alternatives.label: Keep the crunch
alternatives.title: Freshly washed cabbage, carrot or cucumber
alternatives.note: Prepare with clean hands and utensils and eat the salad promptly.

alternatives.label: Takeaway check
alternatives.title: Ask for no raw garnish
alternatives.note: Bean sprouts may be added after cooking, so ask for them fully cooked or left out.

labelCheck: “Washed” and “ready to eat” do not mean raw sprouts are cooked. Check whether they were heated all the way through.

shortAnswer: Choose the pasteurized version during pregnancy. “Fresh,” “raw,” “farm” or “cold-pressed” does not mean safer.
why: Pasteurization reduces harmful germs without changing the basic type of drink, making this one of the easiest like-for-like swaps.

alternatives.label: Closest match
alternatives.title: Pasteurized milk or juice
alternatives.note: Choose the same flavour or milk type with pasteurization clearly stated on the label.

alternatives.label: At a juice bar
alternatives.title: A sealed pasteurized drink
alternatives.note: If staff cannot confirm treatment and clean handling, choose a labelled packaged option.

alternatives.label: At home
alternatives.title: Whole washed fruit plus water
alternatives.note: This avoids uncertainty about an unlabelled fresh-pressed drink.

labelCheck: Find the word “pasteurized” on the container or ask the producer directly. Refrigeration alone does not pasteurize a drink.

shortAnswer: Choose a different protein or spread during pregnancy. Liver and liver products can contain very high vitamin A, and refrigerated pâté also raises food-safety concerns.
why: This is not a food that becomes a simple everyday choice just by heating it. A different filling avoids both the vitamin-A issue and uncertainty around chilled pâté.

alternatives.label: For a main meal
alternatives.title: Freshly cooked meat, fish, egg or beans
alternatives.note: Choose a protein that is cooked thoroughly and fits the rest of your diet.

alternatives.label: For a spread
alternatives.title: Hummus or bean spread
alternatives.note: Use a fresh refrigerated product within its date and keep it cold.

alternatives.label: For iron concerns
alternatives.title: Ask for a tailored iron plan
alternatives.note: Do not use liver or a high-dose supplement to self-treat suspected anaemia.

labelCheck: Check multivitamins and supplements for retinol or high-dose vitamin A too; ask before using them in pregnancy.
